# Adam Hickey

> Senior digital designer in Minneapolis, Minnesota. Visual ideas, beautifully brought to life: twenty years of brand identity, illustration, visual systems and thoughtfully crafted digital experiences, designed and often built by the same hands. Eight years as a graphic designer and front-end developer at three Minneapolis studios (ByDesign, LEVEL, Pixel Farm), thirteen years bringing visual coherence to large enterprise products and design systems at RBA, and now independent projects made end to end. Four things he brings to a creative team: finding the creative idea, building the visual language, bringing the brand into digital, and refining until it feels finished. Open to a senior digital, visual or interactive design role, in Minneapolis, hybrid or remote.

Contact: adam@adamhickey.com. LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/adamdhickey/

Every page is plain HTML with its content in the markup; nothing is rendered by script. Each page carries a canonical URL, an Open Graph card and a schema.org graph, and https://adamhickey.com/sitemap.xml lists every page with a last-modified date.

## Selected work

- [Innovators Studio](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/innovators-studio-visual-identity.html): an identity that made a global innovation network feel like one place. Lead designer, with a marketing manager and a production designer, over four fiscal years: identity, illustration and badges; presentation, newsletter and podcast templates; campaigns, one-pagers and business-model tools; a community portal, an innovators directory and a learning academy. The one measured figure, campaign production time roughly halved by the template library, comes from a small sample of timesheets and is a direction rather than a precise number.
- [Say When](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/say-when.html): a self-initiated, fictional coffee brand concept, made to show the whole arc from strategy to an interactive experience. Specialty coffee without the specialist vocabulary: the pour as the gesture, everyone's own "when" as the idea; naming, logo exploration and identity; three products that are a family without being recolors (First Pour, Second Pour, Last Pour); a campaign; and a working storefront with a plain-language coffee finder at https://adamhickey.com/say-when/index.html. No client, no research study, no sales; nothing is for sale and the checkout is simulated.
- [Door County Found](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/door-county-found.html): a travel guide that feels like advice from someone who knows the place. A vintage-inspired editorial identity (cream paper, harbor navy, beacon gold), a smaller trusted selection, writing in the family's voice, real photography of real places, dog-friendly discovery, and a map in the background; built so his sister keeps it current through a web form. Live at https://doorcountyfound.com.
- [Lucy Learns](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/lucy-learns.html): dog training doesn't happen at a desk. An illustrated, glance-readable training app for his own household: one task a screen, type readable from across the room, the same dog in the same home on every picture, built for one hand and for a stand. The voice-command version failed because the dog took the prompts as cues; a timer replaced it; a teleprompter is a concept, not shipped. Live at https://adamdhickey-collab.github.io/lucy-learns/.
- [The studio years](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/hybrid-designer.html): eight years of brand-led sites, campaigns and apps at ByDesign, LEVEL and Pixel Farm, 2005 to 2013: Lund Boats, Fulton Beer, Hazelden, Northern Spark, Learn to Live (identity, illustration and site), Feed Friendsy, Dorsey and Whitney, and the Pixel Farm family of sites.
- [While We're Here](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/while-were-here.html): a 300mm square hardcover of essays, designed and produced end to end from HTML and CSS through a paged-media engine.
- [Faunaform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/faunaform.html): a screen-print studio for Minnesota wildlife art, in progress: seven animals, one for each hour of a day, art-directed from written briefs to an image model and made printable by software he built; nothing is printed yet and the page says which pictures are simulations.

## Enterprise work

- [Making 40+ enterprise apps feel like one product](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/sap-product-maturity.html): visual coherence, hierarchy and a shared design language across a global corporation's SAP Fiori suite, under one design system and accessibility standard.
- [Grant tools unified into one trusted platform](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/usda-operational-overhead.html): clarity and trust in the USDA-backed Nutrition Incentive Hub, which replaced spreadsheets.
- [One real-time view of a 450+ truck fleet](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/dispatch-complexity.html): dense, fast-changing information made readable for Midwest Couriers' dispatchers.
- [13 years designing enterprise software](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/enterprise-consulting.html): the RBA years, 2013 to 2026, for CBRE, Toro, Banner Bank and International Trucks.
- [How I built this site](https://adamhickey.com/case-study/this-site.html): plain HTML with no framework and no build step, three token files under four normative specs, and eleven checks that measure the rendered page before anything ships.

## Experiments

Prototypes and technical explorations, AI included, from an earlier focus on how designers and coding agents work together. The index is at https://adamhickey.com/lab/index.html.

- [Agent Review](https://adamhickey.com/lab/agent-review.html): a case study with a working React prototype and a public Storybook, following one feature through six stages in which a designer directs a coding agent and decides what ships. Everything in it is simulated and labeled so.
- [Dispatch Cockpit](https://adamhickey.com/prototype/dispatch-cockpit.html): an AI recommendation the dispatcher can check and overrule, interactive, on synthetic data.
- [Designing motion with Claude Code](https://adamhickey.com/lab/designing-motion.html): a scroll-driven motion study.

The index is at https://adamhickey.com/writing/index.html.
